maker: Ole-Johan Dahl and Kristen Nygaard, Norwegian Computing Center
summary: The language that invented classes, objects and inheritance, made by Ole-Johan Dahl and Kristen Nygaard in Norway to write simulations. Smalltalk, C++ and Java all grew from its ideas.

image.alt: Pages from a SIMULA language handbook

events.note: Dahl and Nygaard start designing a language for simulation.
SIMULA I becomes fully operational on a UNIVAC 1107.

events.label: Simula 67
events.note: Simula 67, with classes and inheritance, is formally standardised.

events.label: Last standard
events.note: Simula Standard 1986 is the final revision.

events.label: Turing Award
events.note: Dahl and Nygaard receive the 2001 Turing Award for Simula.

note: Little used, but the origin of classes and objects.
